sentiment.rationale: Full-year comparable EPS guidance was raised from 7%-8% to 8%-9%, but the increase is explicitly attributed to a lower effective tax rate (19.9% vs. prior estimate), not to improved underlying operational performance. Organic revenue guidance (4%-5%) and currency-neutral EPS guidance (6%-7%) were reaffirmed unchanged. Management's tone is confident but acknowledges persistent risks from geopolitical tensions and commodity pressures. The guidance raise is real but mechanically driven by a tax rate change, not organic momentum, so the score is moderately positive but capped below +0.5.

summary.revenue: Organic revenue growth of 10% in Q1 2026, driven by 3% unit case growth and positive pricing, partially offset by mix headwinds.
summary.eps: Comparable EPS of $0.86, up 18% year-over-year, helped by a 3% currency tailwind and higher equity income.
summary.guidance: Full-year 2026: organic revenue growth expected in the 4%-5% range; comparable currency-neutral EPS growth (ex-acquisitions and divestitures) of 6%-7%; comparable EPS growth now guided to 8%-9% versus $3 in 2025, up from prior 7%-8% estimate due to a reduced effective tax rate of 19.9%.
summary.margin: Comparable gross margin declined approximately 30 basis points due to commodity pressures in tea and coffee and inventory timing. Comparable operating margin expanded approximately 70 basis points, as operating expense efficiencies offset the gross margin decline.
key_risks: Geopolitical tensions and regional conflicts (e.g., Middle East) causing volume declines in Eurasia and Middle East in March.
Commodity pressures in tea and coffee expected to persist through the year.
Divestiture headwinds: pending Coca-Cola Beverages Africa sale projected to be a 4-point headwind to comparable net revenues and a 1-point headwind to comparable EPS.
Calendar shift: Q4 2026 will have 6 fewer days compared to Q4 2025.
Ongoing IRS dispute with no resolution date.
key_opportunities: Strong brand activation and innovation (e.g., Coca-Cola Zero-Zero relaunch in Europe, Sprite and Fuze Tea innovations) driving double-digit volume growth for Fuze Tea.
Market and channel expansion: system added more than 600,000 outlets and placed over 340,000 units of cold drink equipment.
FIFA World Cup activations expected to drive volume and consumer engagement.
Revenue growth management (RGM) capabilities and cross-enterprise procurement providing cost mitigation and margin resilience.
Digital consumer engagement (e.g., connected packaging) driving transaction growth and market insights.

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management states 'We are off to a good start this year' and 'I'm confident we are well positioned to deliver on our updated 2026 guidance,' while acknowledging external complexity.

evidence.claim: Full-year comparable EPS guidance was raised from 7%-8% to 8%-9%.
evidence.quote: All in, we now expect comparable earnings per share growth of 8% to 9% versus $3 in 2025, which is an increase from our prior estimate of 7% to 8% due to the lower effective tax rate.

evidence.claim: The guidance raise is attributed to a lower effective tax rate, not organic operational improvement.
evidence.quote: Based on the latest analysis of our global operations, our underlying effective tax rate for 2026 is now expected to be 19.9%, which is a 1 point reduction versus our previous estimate. All in, we now expect comparable earnings per share growth of 8% to 9% versus $3 in 2025, which is an increase from our prior estimate of 7% to 8% due to the lower effective tax rate.

evidence.claim: Organic revenue guidance was reaffirmed unchanged at 4%-5%.
evidence.quote: We continue to expect organic revenue growth of 4% to 5%.

evidence.claim: Comparable currency-neutral EPS guidance (ex-acquisitions and divestitures) was reaffirmed at 6%-7%.
evidence.quote: We now expect growth in comparable currency-neutral earnings per share, excluding acquisitions and divestitures of 6% to 7%.
First quarter comparable EPS of $0.86 increased 18% year-over-year, helped by 3% currency tailwinds.

evidence.claim: Comparable gross margin declined approximately 30 basis points.
evidence.quote: Comparable gross margin declined approximately 30 basis points, stemming primarily from commodity pressures in our tea and coffee businesses, phasing of inventory costs and timing of trade spend.

evidence.claim: Comparable operating margin expanded approximately 70 basis points.
evidence.quote: Comparable operating margin increased approximately 70 basis points, as we've realized operating expense efficiencies while investing further behind our brands.

evidence.claim: Geopolitical tensions and regional conflicts are a stated risk.
evidence.quote: Uncertainty stemming from geopolitical tensions may cause this outlook to change.

evidence.claim: Commodity pressures in tea and coffee are expected to persist.
evidence.quote: We have had commodity pressures in the tea and coffee space, and that's going to continue somewhat through the year.

evidence.claim: Divestiture headwinds from CCBA sale are projected.
evidence.quote: Divestitures are expected to continue to be an approximate 4-point headwind to comparable net revenues and an approximate 1 point headwind to comparable earnings per share. This assumes the pending sale of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa, which is subject to regulatory approvals, closes during the second half of 2026.

evidence.claim: Calendar shift will reduce Q4 2026 days by 6.
evidence.quote: As a reminder, due to a calendar shift, the fourth quarter will have 6 fewer days compared to the fourth quarter of 2025.

evidence.claim: Ongoing IRS dispute is a risk.
evidence.quote: We're continuing to judiciously manage our balance sheet as we await a court decision related to our ongoing dispute with the IRS.

evidence.claim: Innovation and brand activation are key opportunities.
evidence.quote: Coca-Cola Zero-Zero had a strong trial, positive repeat rates and contributed to the trademark of a Coca-Cola growing volume in Europe. ... Globally, Fuze Tea grew volume double digit.

evidence.claim: Market and channel expansion is a growth driver.
evidence.quote: In the past year, our system added more than 600,000 outlets, which increased outlet coverage. ... our system also placed over 340,000 units of cold drink equipment.

evidence.claim: FIFA World Cup activations are expected to drive volume.
evidence.quote: We actually started to execute that in Q1. It was another great decision by our operators with the bottlers in North America and Mexico that you've mentioned as well in Latin America. Both of these regions decided to go head on and start the activation of FIFA World Cup in the Q1.

evidence.claim: RGM capabilities and cross-enterprise procurement provide cost mitigation.
evidence.quote: We have our RGM capabilities as Henrique just pointed out, we have our cross-enterprise procurement group that works with the vast majority of our system partners on both resiliency and productivity initiatives.

evidence.claim: Digital consumer engagement is a differentiator.
evidence.quote: Direct digital consumer engagement—such as connected packaging for promotional activations—was referenced as a key differentiator in driving transaction growth and gathering market insights.
We are off to a good start this year. ... I'm confident we are well positioned to deliver on our updated 2026 guidance.

review_flags.reason: The guidance raise is entirely attributed to a lower tax rate, not operational improvement. A human reviewer should confirm whether this mechanical raise warrants a score of +0.30 or if a lower score (e.g., +0.15) is more appropriate given the lack of organic momentum.
